findings.finding: Q3 2026 has a two-currency bar that does not reconcile: US$ consensus $0.49-0.50 adjusted EPS translates at the Q3 average USD/BRL of roughly 5.1-5.3 to about R$2.50-2.65 per share, i.e. ~R$600-630M of adjusted net income on ~238M weighted shares (Q2 239.5M less buybacks), while the two Brazilian broker previews sit at R$553M (Safra) and R$571M (Itau BBA), i.e. ~R$2.30-2.40; a print in line with the BRL previews reads as a ~5-10% headline miss against the US$ number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-13): adjusted NI R$582.7M, -2.6% y/y, revenue $709.4M vs $731.2M est, stock -6.65% (baseline). Q1 2026: EPS ~3.9% below consensus, stock about -0.9% (aggregator pages, low quality). Q3 2025: bottom-line beat and EPS guide raise, stock still -7.3% (Seeking Alpha / iTiger headlines).
findings.why_not_priced: The US$ consensus aggregators (Zacks, EW) show $0.49-0.50, implying 14% y/y EPS growth; if the BRL previews were in the US$ number it would read ~$0.44-0.46. The translation is an inference by this searcher from share count and FX, not a published reconciliation.
findings.independence: Share count from the Q2 6-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1745431/000207097926000275/stoneco_earningsrelease2q2.htm, 239.5M basic weighted); US$ bar from https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/STNE/22948. Proxy/inference; FX average is approximate (July close R$5.08 https://www.opovo.com.br/noticias/economia/2026/07/24/o-dolar-a-vista-fechou-em-recuo-de-006-a-rs-508-em-desvantagem-contra-o-real.html).

findings.finding: The FY2026 adjusted EPS guide (R$10.80-11.40) is out of reach on the previews: H1 adjusted EPS was R$4.58, so the low end needs R$6.22 in H2 (R$3.11 a quarter) against a Q3 preview of ~R$2.30-2.40; even a strong Q4 leaves FY2026 near R$9.5-10, ~10% below the bottom of the range, so a cut or a 'below the range' statement is close to arithmetically forced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: March 2026 (Q4 2025 print with first 2026 guide judged conservative): stock -19.4% (https://www.tikr.com/blog/stoneco-stock-tumbles-19-after-earnings-report-what-the-2026-outlook-means-for-investors). August 2026, guide kept but steered to the low end: -6.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Itau BBA already cut its 2026 estimate 10% and the US$ FY consensus ($2.27) still sits above the top of the guide, so aggregated consensus has not caught up. If fully priced, FY2026 US$ consensus would sit below $2.07, not above $2.19.
findings.independence: H1 EPS arithmetic from https://finsee.ai/earnings/stne/2026/q2/en/ (R$4.58 H1, R$3.11/qtr needed); previews from Finsiders (Itau BBA, Safra). Shares the preview document with finding 1 but lands on a different line (full-year guide, not the quarter).

findings.finding: The 2027 guide (adjusted EPS R$11.8-13.4, gross profit R$7.2-8.3B) was set before Lula's re-election; since then the BRL fell 8.2% in a day (R$5.40), the yield curve steepened ~250bp (UBS), and Copom held Selic at 13.75% on 2026-11-04 against a 39-of-75 survey expecting a cut to 13.50%, so a 2027 cut, withdrawal or a 'rates higher for longer' reset is the most likely new information on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this name has traded hardest on: -19.4% on the March 2026 guide; Aug 2026 low-end steer -6.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced in level (stock ~3-4x pre-cut earnings, -31% in 20 days, UBS PT $8.50 vs $7.83 spot), but the size of the reset is unknown and the company has not spoken since 2026-08-13 (no 6-K since then on EDGAR). If fully priced the stock would not have rallied +4.5% over the five days into the print.
findings.independence: Copom hold: https://www.oliberal.com/economia/bc-copom-interrompe-ciclo-de-calibracao-e-mantem-taxa-selic-em-13-75-ao-ano-1.1190560 (2026-11-04). FX: https://tribunadosertao.com.br/geral/2026/10/26/1006774-dolar-sobe-821-e-bolsa-cai-1388-apos-reeleicao-de-lula. 2027 guide: https://quartr.com/events/stoneco-ltd-stne-q2-2026_3YnSTMSB. Macro-to-company transmission, not confirmed by the company.

findings.finding: Capital return lever at a depressed price: StoneCo committed to return >R$2B of excess capital through buybacks during 2026, spent R$739M in Q2 alone and repurchased its previous program at an average US$16.34; the stock is now $7.83 (market cap ~$1.9B, ~R$10B), so any acceleration or new program on the call would retire a much larger share of the float per real spent; constraint: adjusted net cash fell to R$1.35B after the R$3.08B May dividend and managerial Tier 1 is 26.3% 'normalized'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: March 2026 print carried a large repurchase plan and still fell -19.4% on the guide; capital return has not been enough to offset a guidance disappointment on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: No 6-K or buyback notice since 2026-08-13 (EDGAR list), and the company entered its quiet period 2026-10-28, two days after the crash, so it has said nothing on capital since the price halved. Previews (EW) mention buybacks only as 'quiet support' with no amount.
findings.independence: 2026 commitment of >R$2B buybacks: https://www.prnewswire.com/br/comunicados-para-a-imprensa/stone-bate-guidances-de-2025-e-fecha-o-ano-com-r-3-bilhoes-de-excesso-de-capital-distribuidos-aos-acionistas-302701672.html; prior program average price: https://www-web.itiger.com/news/2593445849. Market cap from https://fool.com/investing/2026/10/26/why-stoneco-stock-crashed-today.

findings.finding: Credit was deteriorating into Q3: at Q2 the 15-90 day NPL rose to 6.00% from 4.97% and >90 day to 8.60% from 6.98%, coverage fell to 204% from 229% (265% a year ago), the book grew 16% q/q to R$3.75B, and a R$200M off-adjusted provision was taken on a distressed card issuer (likely Will Bank per BTG); the rising early bucket points to higher >90 NPLs in Q3, and ABECS reported ~10% revolving-card default in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 credit deterioration triggered Citi's downgrade to Neutral (PT $18->$11, 2026-05-15, https://www.portaltela.com/noticias/economia/2026/05/15/citi-corta-recomendacao-e-aponta-deterioracao-do-credito-da-stone/); Q2 with NPLs up: -6.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: previews assume cost of risk ~21% (Itau BBA), i.e. flat, while the Q2 early-bucket NPL jump argues for higher provisions; management guided cost of risk falling to the high teens by year end. A further one-off issuer provision would sit outside adjusted numbers.
findings.independence: ABECS Q3 card data with ~10% revolving default: https://eshoje.com.br/?p=908211 (2026-11-10). BTG attribution of the issuer: https://finsidersbrasil.com.br/noticias-sobre-fintechs/stone-perde-controle-da-inadimplencia-e-ve-atrasos-acima-de-90-dias-dispararem/. Cost-of-risk guide from Quartr summary.

findings.finding: Industry card volumes decelerated in Q3: ABECS (2026-11-10) reported total card spend +6.6% y/y vs +7.7% in Q2 and +8.3% in Q1, with credit +10% and debit/prepaid falling, and cut its 2026 growth range to 7.5-9.5% from 9.5-11.5%; Safra expects StoneCo card volume -1.8% y/y with TPV R$147B, Itau BBA TPV +5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: stock reportedly rose on a TPV beat despite an EPS miss; Q2 TPV +4.3% accelerated and the stock still fell -6.65% on earnings/guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Released two days before the print and after most previews (Finsiders 2026-11-03, EW 2026-11-04); a broad industry series, so sized small as a proxy.
findings.independence: Same ABECS release reported by https://forbes.com.br/forbes-money/2026/11/transacoes-cartoes-12-trilhao-terceiro-trimestre/; Safra TPV view in Finsiders 2026-11-03. Industry proxy; StoneCo is MSMB- and debit-heavy.

findings.finding: Q3 funding costs fell: Copom cut Selic five times through 2026-09-16 (to 14% in August, 13.75% in September), so average CDI in Q3 was below Q2's 14.4% (Q1 14.9%); the Q2 release already credited lower CDI with reducing financial expenses sequentially, which should cushion Q3 margins even as deposit float revenue declines.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 benefited from lower CDI and still fell -6.65%; this line has not driven the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced into previews (Itau BBA still expects higher financial expenses), filed as a small offset because the Q3 rate path was falling while the market now trades the post-election forward path.
findings.independence: CDI 14.9%->14.4% and its effect on financial expenses: Q2 6-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1745431/000207097926000275/stoneco_earningsrelease2q2.htm.

findings.finding: Expectations have been reset hard before the print: stock -31% in 20 sessions and 5.9% above its 52-week low, ~3-4x forward earnings on pre-election estimates (TIKR), UBS cut to Neutral with an $8.50 target on 2026-11-05, Citi already Neutral, Itau BBA cut 2026 estimates 10%, and Earnings Whispers bearish sentiment ~9%; the macro drawdown was not company news (Finanztrends: 'not a new operating report').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print came after a macro drawdown of this size; the last four prints all fell, but each came off a higher starting multiple (5.2x before the election per TIKR, 15.3x five-year average).
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price; filed because it sets the bar for the guidance negatives. If the reset were incomplete, the stock would not have bounced +4.5% in the five sessions after the UBS downgrade and the Copom hold.
findings.independence: https://www.finanztrends.de/news/stoneco-aktie-absturz-nach-lulas-wiederwahl/ (2026-10-26); UBS note via goldesel 2026-11-05; sentiment via https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/STNE/22948.

baseline_tension: The negatives (guide cut forced, 2027 reset, credit) agree with the -31% run-up and a name that has sold its last four prints, so they are largely in the price; the cut-against is the reset itself and an unexercised buyback lever at half the last repurchase price, which is why p_up sits at 44 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5/6 (inference vs document, verify the bar): the two-currency bar finding is a searcher inference from FX and share count, cut from -0.8 to -0.6; the US$ bar itself has two agreeing sources so no cap on the rest.

'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism' plus lesson 3 (caveat reaches the number): the negative set is widely previewed and the stock is at its 52w low after a reset, so p_up moved from 42 to 44 and expected_move from -1.44 to -1.08.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (6.95% of float, 2.5 DTC, May 2026, stale); not crowded, negatives left at their size.
Rebuilt the reaction base rate from confirmed releases per 'a reaction history built from the wrong events is worse than none'; this was done before the file was read and did not change sizes.
